pr.title: Have init allow every project command except init, upgrade, and config changes
pr.head: 18cd80f775f13220369d0399cf3ff6cdde0393dd

summary: project init writes permission rules into your own Claude Code settings (~/.claude/settings.json) and your Codex rules (~/.codex/rules/projector.rules). Those rules decide which project commands an agent can run without a prompt or a refusal from the host's automatic approval, such as Claude Code's auto mode or Codex's approval reviewer. Until this change, init allowed only three commands: project review publish, project review hold, and project summary publish. Every other project command could stop for a prompt, which pushes agents toward editing Projector's files by hand or calling gh api directly.

This change allows every project command and asks only before the few that the author judges to reach outside Projector's own state. The two hosts get different shapes of rule, because their rule languages differ:

HostAllowedStill asks or falls through
Claude CodeBash(project *) in permissions.allowproject init, project upgrade, project config set and unset, and any command line that starts with an option, such as project --root . init, through rules in permissions.ask
CodexEach top-level command by name, plus config get, list, and pathsinit, upgrade, config set and unset, and any line that starts with an option match no rule and fall to Codex's usual approval
init also removes the older, narrower allow rules it wrote before, and only from permissions.allow. The documentation and three skills now describe the broad rule.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Allow rule: a host setting that runs a matching command with no prompt and, in Claude Code's auto mode, no classifier check.
  • Ask rule: a Claude Code setting that prompts for a matching command. Claude Code checks ask rules before allow rules, so an ask rule wins.
  • prefix_rule: a Codex rule that matches a command's first words exactly, with no wildcard.
  • Superseded rules: the narrow allow rules, such as Bash(project review publish *), that Bash(project *) now covers.

cards.title: Open review findings
cards.html:
• P1: project site build and serve run any shell command given with --prepare, and --allow-prepare self-approves a repository's site.prepare. Both now run without a prompt.
  • P2: project inbox answer and dismiss record the person's answer to an agent's question, and are now allowed without a prompt.

groups.title: The rules init writes
groups.kicker: What each host now allows, asks for, and drops
intro: src/projector/permissions.py holds the rules as constants and the two functions that write them. ALLOW is the one Claude Code allow rule, ASK the five Claude Code ask rules, and SUPERSEDED the narrow rules that init removes. CODEX_PATTERNS builds the Codex file, which init rewrites whole.

Bash(project -*) exists because the CLI accepts --root and --projects-dir before the command name. Without it, project --root . init would match the allow rule and none of the command ask rules. Codex has no wildcard to express the same thing, which is why the Codex side lists allowed commands instead of listing ones to ask for.

tests/test_permissions.py pins one table of command lines to the decision each host reaches, and a test fails when the parser gains a top-level command that the Codex list neither allows nor leaves out on purpose.

checks.text: The question to hold while reading: does every command the broad rule now allows stay inside Projector's own state? The excluded set is init, upgrade, and config set and unset. The review found two more commands that reach outside it, flagged on the constants below.

files.note: The rule constants, the Claude settings rewrite that adds ASK and drops SUPERSEDED, and the Codex file template.

checks.text: Open P1 finding: Bash(project *), and site in CODEX_COMMANDS, allow project site build --prepare '<any command>' and project site serve --prepare, which run that command through the shell. --allow-prepare also lets an agent approve a cloned repository's own site.prepare command, the step that exists so the person decides. The review reproduced the --prepare case at this head. The finding asks for ask rules on site build and site serve, and a Codex entry that allows only page, status, and workflow.

Open P2 finding: the allow rule covers project inbox answer and dismiss, which record the person's answer to an agent's question. The band delivers that answer to the asking agent as the person's decision, so an agent can answer its own question. The finding asks for ask rules on both, and a Codex inbox entry that leaves them out.

Superseded rules leave only permissions.allow. The review ran init against a scratch HOME whose settings held two narrow allow rules and a narrow rule in deny: the allow rules were replaced by Bash(project *), the deny entry and existing ask entries stayed, and a second run printed unchanged.

files.note: The decision table for both hosts, and the test that ties the Codex list to the parser.

checks.text: This row pins project site serve as allowed in both hosts. The P1 finding on permissions.py would change it to ask and none.

groups.title: init and review rules
groups.kicker: The CLI's callers of the rules and their messages
intro: project init and project review rules call allow_commands, the renamed allow_publish. review rules only reports, so a review loop can learn before its first publish that the rules are missing. The messages now describe Projector's commands in general instead of naming three.
tests/test_projector.py replaces the three-rule expectations with a granted() helper and adds tests for the superseded rules and for ask rules added beside an existing allow rule.

files.note: The rename to allow_commands and reworded help and refusal messages; no behavior change beyond the rules themselves.
Settings fixtures move to granted(); new tests cover removal of superseded rules and the report-only path.

groups.kicker: What readers and agents are told about the new rules
intro: docs/cli.md lists the ask rules, explains why Bash(project -*) exists, and shows the Codex file. The README and the fix-pr, review-pr, and start-review-loop skills now refer to Bash(project *) instead of the narrow rules.
